summary.text: 字 now means a written character or word. Its structure points toward an older association with raising or nurturing a child: 子, “child,” stands beneath 宀, a roof. 子 also supplies sound, so the image and the pronunciation both matter to the supplied explanation of its construction.

history.text: The Shuowen describes 子 under 宀 and explicitly says that 子 also gives the sound. Dong Chinese connects the roof with nurturing, then sketches a development through education to words and writing. This makes the older household association intelligible, even though the later change in meaning needs qualification.

uncertainties.text: The route from nurturing to “written character” is not settled in the excerpts. Wiktionary allows either a derivation from producing or generating, or a different word root. The education sequence is therefore one account, not a demonstrated chain of semantic changes.
